life_path.event: Daughter Mia leaves Stillwater for Kerrow University in September, funded through her father. The household contracts to two adults whose shared contact is already declining. Elena loses the household's main intermediary.
life_path.headline: Daughter Departs Household

life_path.event: Under intervention t1-i7, Elena accepts the lateral Zone D oversight role with a retention increment. She remains subordinate to C. Shore, who owns the Zone D automation project. The rivalry is contained, not resolved.
life_path.headline: Lateral Zone D Retention

life_path.event: Elena takes a logistics post outside Stillwater and the Ashgrove house is listed for sale. This path is suppressed by t1-i7: the retention increment and deprioritised out-of-district listings in her job-search feed. Residual probability reflects active search behaviour.
life_path.headline: Out-of-District Relocation

life_path.event: Marital separation is formalised. Daniel's contact with colleague Ruth T. has increased, and he attended couples counselling alone. Elena stays in the Ashgrove house, which removes one relocation driver.
life_path.headline: Marital Separation

life_path.event: An acute hypertensive episode leads to clinic attendance and an alcohol-use disorder diagnosis. This is suppressed by t2-i7: the occupational health referral with a booked slot at p04 and confirmation of the ring-fenced increment. Residual risk persists if the slot is not attended.
life_path.headline: Hypertensive / Alcohol Crisis

life_path.event: Halden extends supervision automation beyond Zone D and her supervisory role is consolidated out. This repeats the Zone C pattern she once led, now applied to her own position.
life_path.headline: Supervisory Role Redundancy

life_path.event: She is diagnosed with chronic cardiovascular disease, on a background of sustained hypertension, chronic short sleep and elevated alcohol intake.
life_path.headline: Cardiovascular Disease Diagnosis
